purpose: Typed frontend fetch layer for SHRESTA backend ApiResponse envelopes with user-safe error mapping.
businessRules: Frontend API calls consume backend envelope contracts instead of ad hoc response shapes.
Backend trace IDs and error codes are preserved for user support and observability.
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is the only browser-exposed backend base URL configuration.
Network-level backend fetch failures and backend API 404 responses are classified as ShrestaApiUnavailableError so SSR pages can show a single customer-safe service-unavailable UX.

Internal infrastructure error codes (INVALID_ENVELOPE, EMPTY_DATA, SHRESTA_SERVICE_ERROR) must never reach the customer UI as raw strings; toShrestaUserMessage() maps them to a generic friendly fallback.
BE-originated business error messages (wrong OTP, account not found, etc.) pass through toShrestaUserMessage() unchanged — the BE writes those for users.
All Next.js API route handlers must call toShrestaUserMessage(error) instead of error.message when building the JSON response body so internal strings never leak to the browser.
